Register exact: `_DAT_40010c14=0x1000` (GPIOB_BRR, PB12 CS LOW), then FUN_0802f0c4(0x90) sends command 0x90, three FUN_0802f0c4(0) dummy/address bytes, two FUN_0802f0b8() (=0802f0c4(0xFF)) reads, then `_DAT_40010c10=0x1000` (GPIOB_BSRR, PB12 CS HIGH). FUN_0802f0c4 is the full-duplex byte engine: poll SPI2.SR(0x40003808) TXE(bit1) via 0803683c, write SPI2_DR(_DAT_4000380c=0x4000380c), poll RXNE(bit0), return DR&0xff. So STOCK USES W25 command 0x90 = 'Read Manufacturer/Device ID' (needs 3 address bytes, returns 2 bytes mfr+dev). OUR firmware (flash_fs.c:293) uses command 0x9F = JEDEC ID (no address, returns 3 bytes mfr/type/capacity). Same SPI2 peripheral, same PB12 CS-low/high framing (CS_ASSERT=GPIOB->clr PIN12 == BRR; CS_DEASSERT=GPIOB->scr == BSRR — polarity matches stock exactly), same TXE/RXNE polling structure. The ID command and byte count intentionally differ — ours is a richer JEDEC read used by the `flash jedec` debug command (usb_debug.c:835).
r1.next_action: DIVERGENT by design (0x9F vs 0x90) — both correctly identify the W25Q128, ours returns capacity too. Not a faithfulness defect. To mark equivalence-faithful you'd reimplement the 0x90 path, but there's no functional reason; keep R1. Bench check: `flash jedec` USB-debug cmd should return EF/40/18.

r1.name: spi2_init
r1.our_impl: firmware/src/drivers/flash_fs.c:58 flash_fs_raw_spi_init_once (clocks :64-66, GPIO :68-90, SPI :93-98)
r1.findings: Stock = SPI2 master bring-up, 256 bytes. Register exact decode: (1) RCC clock enables via FUN_0802a514 (base 0x40021000): 0x1c000e -> RCC_APB1ENR(+0x1C) bit14 = SPI2EN; 0x180000 -> RCC_APB2ENR(+0x18) bit0 = AFIOEN; 0x180003 -> APB2ENR bit3 = GPIOBEN (called for the GPIOB pins). (2) GPIO config via FUN_080302fc(0x40010c00=GPIOB,&initstruct) four times for pins 0x1000/0x2000/0x4000/0x8000 = PB12/13/14/15, with mode/cnf nibbles (0x18=output 50MHz, 0x10=input variants) written into GPIOB_CRH (param_1[1], 0x40010c04) — 080302fc is a faithful STM32 GPIO_Init that sets 4-bit mode|cnf per pin. (3) SPI2 peripheral init via FUN_08036848(0x40003800,..) setting CR1 (master, CPOL/CPHA, baud, NSS=software) and FUN_08036830 setting CR1 bit0x40=SPE. (4) FUN_0802eee8() JEDEC/ID probe at the end. OUR flash_fs_raw_spi_init_once mirrors this register-for-register on AT32 HAL: enables CRM_GPIOB+CRM_IOMUX(AFIO)+CRM_SPI2 clocks (:64-66 == the three RCC bits), configures PB13=SCK/PB15=MOSI as MUX push-pull, PB14=MISO input, PB12=CS GPIO output (:72-89 — same four PB12-15 pins as stock), then SPI2->ctrl1 = master|/16-prescaler|software-NSS-high, SPE enable (:93-98 == 08036848+08036830). Pin assignment, peripheral, CS-on-PB12, and master/software-NSS topology all match stock.
r1.next_action: Equivalence confirmed by reading both. Minor non-faithful detail: stock's exact baud prescaler and CPOL/CPHA come from 08036848's CR1 word (not re-derived here) while ours hardcodes mode-0 /16 — both valid for W25Q reads. Bench: any flash read (jedec/raw) succeeding proves init correct; already exercised via usb_debug flash cmds.

r1.name: gpio_pin_config
r1.our_impl: firmware/src/drivers/flash_fs.c:68-89 gpio_init() calls (AT32 HAL gpio_init equivalent); same pattern in fpga.c/lcd.c/button_scan.c init
r1.findings: Stock = STM32F1-style GPIO_Init, 482 bytes. Full decode: param_1=GPIO base (param_1[0]=CRL@+0x00, param_1[1]=CRH@+0x04), param_2=GPIO_InitTypeDef (param_2[0]=pin bitmask, byte[5]=mode, byte[6]/byte[7]+param_2[2]=speed/cnf bits). It computes the 4-bit config nibble `uVar3`: if speed-byte==0x28/0x18 it's an AF/output-50MHz case storing the bias into param_1[5]/[4] (BSRR/BRR pre-set) and nibble=8; else input/output cnf assembled from (byte7&3)+(param2[2]&4)+(byte&8). Then for each set bit in the low byte of pinmask it clears the matching 4-bit field in CRL and ORs in uVar3 (8 unrolled `if (uVar2<<n)<0` tests for pins 0-7), and for the high byte advances to CRH (param_1+1) doing pins 8-15. This is exactly the classic STM32F1 `GPIO_Init` CRL/CRH 4-bits-per-pin algorithm. OUR firmware never reimplements this primitive directly — it calls the AT32 HAL `gpio_init(GPIOx, &gpio_init_type)` (flash_fs.c:76/82/89, and identically in fpga.c, lcd.c, button_scan.c), which performs the same CRL/CRH 4-bit mode|cnf programming on the register-compatible AT32 GPIO block. Functionally identical register effect (mode/cnf nibbles per pin), just sourced from the vendor HAL rather than hand-rolled.
r1.next_action: Equivalence confirmed: AT32 gpio_init == stock 080302fc at the CRL/CRH register level (AT32 GPIO is STM32F1-register-compatible per CLAUDE.md). No reimplementation owed — using the HAL is the faithful equivalent. Verified by every peripheral (SPI2/SPI3/LCD/buttons) coming up correctly on bench.

r1.name: gpio_read_input
r1.our_impl: firmware/src/drivers/button_scan.c:106-169 + drivers/fpga.c:810,2141,2391 (direct ->idt reads)
r1.findings: Stock FUN_080304e0 = `return (*(uint*)(base+8) & mask) == mask` — reads GPIO IDR (offset +8) and returns true only when ALL masked bits are set (GPIO_ReadInputDataBit-style helper). Register-faithful (same peripheral, same +8 IDR offset, same bit mask), just inlined rather than a named one-call helper.

r1.name: spi_check_flag
r1.our_impl: firmware/src/drivers/flash_fs.c:106,114 (TXE then RXNE poll in flash_fs_raw_spi_xfer)
r1.findings: Stock FUN_0803683c = `return (*(uint*)(base+8) & flag) != 0` — reads SPI_SR (offset +8) and tests any masked bit (full_decompile.c:28401). Sole consumer FUN_0802f0c4 (the SPI2 byte-xfer primitive, @21318-21324): `do{}while(check_flag(0x40003800,2)==0)` (wait TXE=bit1) then write DR at 0x4000380C, then `do{}while(check_flag(0x40003800,1)==0)` (wait RXNE=bit0), then read DR. Our flash_fs_raw_spi_xfer (flash_fs.c:103-120) is the same primitive: `while(!(sts & (1U<<1)))` (TXE) -> `->dt = tx` -> `while(!(sts & (1U<<0)))` (RXNE) -> read `->dt`. Same SR offset, same TXE(0x2)/RXNE(0x1) flags, same poll ordering. Ours adds a finite timeout (stock spins forever) — a safety superset, not a behavioral divergence.
r1.next_action: None — equivalence confirmed. SR offset, flag bits, and poll sequence all match stock's byte-xfer loop; our timeout is an additive safety guard.

r1.name: spi_peripheral_init
r1.our_impl: firmware/src/drivers/flash_fs.c:93-97 (ctrl1/ctrl2 literal init)
r1.findings: Stock FUN_08036848 (full_decompile.c:28411-28463) builds SPI_CR1/CR2 bit-by-bit from an 8-byte config struct. Decoding the struct the caller fills (@21238-21245: dir=0,mode=1,presc=0,firstbit=0,datasize=0,cpol=1,cpha=1,nss=1) yields stock CR1 = MSTR(b2) | SSM(b9) | SSI(b8) | CPOL=1(b1) | CPHA=1(b0), 8-bit (DFF=0), MSB-first, prescaler index 0 = /2 (CR2 baud branch untaken). That is SPI MODE 3 at /2 on SPI2 (0x40003800), pins PB12=CS/PB13=SCK/PB14=MISO/PB15=MOSI (GPIOB @0x40010C00, pins 0x1000/0x2000/0x4000/0x8000 — exactly our pinout). Our flash_fs.c:93-97 sets ctrl1 = MSTR | (3<<3 = /16) | SSI | SSM, ctrl2=0, with NO CPOL/CPHA bits => SPI MODE 0 at /16. Same peripheral and pins, but two divergences: clock mode (0 vs stock 3) and prescaler (/16 vs stock /2). For a W25Q128 both mode 0 and mode 3 are valid and /16 is just slower, so it functions — but it is NOT register-faithful to stock.
r1.next_action: To make VERIFY_FAITHFUL, change flash_fs.c:93-96 ctrl1 to set CPOL(1<<1)|CPHA(1<<0) and prescaler 0 (drop the `3<<3`), matching stock mode 3 /2. Otherwise document as an intentional conservative divergence (mode-0 /16 is functionally equivalent for the W25Q128 read path, which our flash_fs_raw_read_bytes @303-339 already mirrors: opcode 0x03 + 3 address bytes + 0xFF dummies = stock FUN_0802f048 @21261).

r1.name: usart_tx_config_writer
r1.our_impl: firmware/src/drivers/fpga.c: usart2_send_cmd (L342), fpga_timed_send_cmd (L390), fpga_wire_send_word (L417), fpga_send_scope_runtime_blocks (L440), fpga_wire_send_bank_words (L422)
r1.findings: Stock 0x08039734 is the upstream encoder that reads scope/meter state (per SCOPE_CMD_PARAMETERS.md it pulls voltage range, coupling, trigger level, timebase from the state struct) and produces a 16-bit wire word (cmd_hi<<8 | cmd_lo) which it queues to usart_tx_queue (0x20002D74, 2-byte items). The DOWNSTREAM frame builder is dvom_tx_task @ 0x080373f4 (decompiled_2C53T_v2.c:30822): it dequeues the 2-byte item, writes byte[2]=cmd_hi (DAT_20000008), byte[3]=cmd_lo (cRam20000007), checksum byte = cmd_hi+cmd_lo (cRam2000000e), then sets USART2 CTRL1 bit 0x80 (TDBEIEN) so the ISR @ 0x080276xx (line 13701-13705) transmits all 10 bytes and clears 0x80 after byte 10. Our firmware faithfully mirrors the FRAME format: fpga.c:344-353 builds a 10-byte frame with frame[2]=cmd_hi, frame[3]=cmd_lo, frame[9]=(cmd_hi+cmd_lo)&0xFF, and fpga_timed_send_cmd queues 2-byte items ((cmd_hi<<8)|cmd_lo) exactly like the stock queue item. DIVERGENCES: (1) our checksum sits at frame[9] vs stock's byte[6]/cRam2000000e position; (2) we poll TDBE (fpga.c:319) instead of stock's ISR-driven TX (CTRL1 0x80); (3) most importantly the config_writer's state->cmd_hi mapping was never fully decoded — SCOPE_CMD_PARAMETERS.md L54 explicitly says 'These cmd_hi values are guesses' and the dispatch table at 0x08044E74 has null entries. Our fpga.c:424-425 hardcodes bank words {0x050C,0x050E,0x0510,0x0511}/{0x050D,0x0517,0x0516,0x0515} and L456-467 builds trigger/timebase words from heuristics, not a byte-exact replica of 0x08039734's encoding.
r1.next_action: Decode 0x08039734's body directly (not present as a discrete FUN_ in either dump — extract via objdump of APP_2C53T_V1.2.0 at flash 0x08039734, 316 bytes) to recover the exact 7 command-type encoders and their per-state cmd_hi tables. Then verify wire equivalence on the bench: Saleae-capture stock USART2 TX during a scope range/timebase/trigger change and diff against our fpga_send_scope_runtime_blocks output. Cannot be VERIFY_FAITHFUL until the FPGA config-entry wall is cleared and live scope data confirms the FPGA accepts our words.

r1.name: scope_read_adc_sample
r1.our_impl: ABSENT (toolchain-provided): GCC libgcc __aeabi_l2f / CMSIS soft-float; our scope ADC path is firmware/src/drivers/fpga.c (0x04/0x05 channel reads) + main.c render, unrelated to this helper
r1.findings: MISNAMED in function_names.md:348 ('scope_read_adc_sample', LOW confidence). FUN_0803ee20 (decompiled_2C53T_v2.c:38455) is NOT an ADC reader — it is a Keil/ARM compiler runtime soft-float helper, specifically signed int64->float32 conversion (__aeabi_l2f / __floatdi2). Register-level proof: takes param_1=low32, param_2=high32 of a 64-bit int; handles two's-complement sign (negate both words, borrow); normalizes the magnitude with LZCOUNT; builds an IEEE-754 single via (sign | 0x3f800000) + 0xf000000 + exponent*0x800000 + mantissa, with round-to-nearest-even (the '(uVar1 & 1) -> & 0xfffffffe' tie-to-even clamp). 0x3f800000 = 1.0f exponent field, 0x800000 = one mantissa LSB per exponent step — textbook i64->f32. Confirmed by its sole call site, fpga_task @ 0x08036xxx (decompiled_2C53T_v2.c:8059): 'fVar73 = (float)FUN_0803ee20(iVar56,iVar46)' — a (float) cast of a 64-bit (lo,hi) difference, sitting beside sibling helpers VectorUnsignedToFloat/VectorSignedToFloat used for the same conversion of 32-bit operands. There is no GPIO/ADC/SPI register access anywhere in the function. It does not belong to the scope acquisition path at all.
r1.next_action: Rename in function_names.md / coverage_ledger.csv from 'scope_read_adc_sample' to 'aeabi_l2f_int64_to_float'. No firmware reimplementation needed: our GCC build links libgcc which supplies the equivalent soft-float (or the M4F VFP does i64->f32 inline). This is a toolchain primitive, justifiably NA. Real scope-ADC sample reads live in our fpga.c per-channel 0x04/0x05 1026-byte reads, which are separately FPGA_BLOCKED but are a different function.
